title: A locally bounded-below derived object on a Noetherian scheme has a uniform lower bound
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $E$ an object of $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose every point has an open neighbourhood on which the restricted cohomology sheaves of $E$ vanish below some integer. Then there is a single integer $a$ such that $E$ is in $D^{\ge a}(\mathcal O_Y)$.

proof.text: Use quasi-compactness to take a finite subcover of the neighbourhoods in the hypothesis. Finset induction using min gives an integer no greater than every local bound, with 0 as the empty-cover bound.

For any degree below this integer, restrict each section of the cohomology sheaf to the intersection with a cover member. Its restriction is zero because the local module sheaf is zero. The underlying abelian sheaf section-extensionality theorem implies the section is zero. Hence the identity morphism of the cohomology sheaf is zero. Use DerivedCategory.isGE_iff to obtain the global lower bound.
